flagged.evidence: Step 1.3 says that from |V(J)|>=|V(G)|^tau, [L4] gives |V(J)|^(1/2)>=|V(G)|^(tau/2). But the cited dependency `thm-real-power-laws` states only equality laws: `a^{r+s}=a^ra^s`, `(ab)^r=a^rb^r`, `(a/b)^r=a^r/b^r`, and `(a^r)^s=a^{rs}`. It does not state monotonicity of x -> x^(1/2) on positive reals, which is the extra fact needed for this inequality transfer.

Step 1.4 concludes from `hom(G)^2>=|V(G)|^tau` that `hom(G)>=|V(G)|^(tau/2)` and cites [L4]. On disk, `thm-real-power-laws` proves only product/quotient/iterated-power equalities, not the monotonicity needed to pass from an inequality between positive reals to an inequality between their square roots. The cited item is therefore too weak for this step as written.

Step 1.1 uses [L4] to pass from `|B_i|>=|V(G)| t^(-1/tau)` to `|B_i|^tau >= (|V(G)| t^(-1/tau))^tau`. The cited dependency `thm-real-power-laws` states only equality laws for positive real powers and does license the final equality `( |V(G)| t^(-1/tau) )^tau = |V(G)|^tau t^(-1)`, but it does not state monotonicity of x -> x^tau for tau>0, which is the missing justification for the preceding inequality.
